doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

chapter: Discovering jazz and the trad band
title: Forming a school jazz band and taking up trombone
summary: After seeing The Glenn Miller Story, he and a friend decided to start a band; he got the trombone, having only played bugle in the Cadet Corps.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you lean towards being a writer even before the music—

I was always good at English, I was always capable when it came to writing, but I hadn’t thought in terms of writing. No, what led me to writing was falling for the music and wanting to play the music. And very early on, about sixteen or seventeen, after this hearing Sidney Bechet on record, I started to think well I must try and do something. And what I remember in particular was “The Glenn Miller Story,” when that came out. My pal and I saw it three times in one week. And I remember to this day walking up, where we lived, and us saying together we’re going to have a band. We hadn’t actually worked out what we were going to play, we hadn’t worked out whether we could ever manage to do it, but we were going to have a band. And we kind of tossed a coin and I got the trombone and he went and got the trumpet and that’s how it started. And we wanted to play. And we found other like minds at school, because we were all at the same school, and we formed a jazz band. And we had a lot of fun. And well, it was probably just an amateur thing but it was great fun and we had a little fun doing it you know.
So you hadn’t played the trombone before that?

I had done no musical study, we didn’t have a piano at home, I just found this desire to play the trombone out of this, well, inspirational moment. And I thought well all you’ve got to do, you pick it up and you blow into it. I’d already played the bugle in the, we had a Cadet Corps, a marching band at school, and I’d played the bugle in that, I’d played the fife, which is a small flute, and I also played the tenor drum. So I was already kind of involved with that kind of musical activity, quite limited, before I’d got some lip, so I’d played the bugle for a number of years, so I knew how to get a note out of the trombone, that was all right. But the difficult bit is about which notes, you know, I had to try to deal with later.
I saw that movie, I can’t begin to tell you how many times. In fact I never forgave you guys for that English Channel thing that he went down in.
Yes. That’s right. It wasn’t our fault, honestly. Although they still think there’s the possibility of finding him one day. They’re still looking down there.
Well did it occur to you at that point that maybe there’s a career for me at some point here?

No. We were just doing this because, it was the time of the English traditional jazz revival, the trad boom, right? That’s the period we’re talking about.
